key_insight: Multi-pin wire-based friction stir welding compensated out-of-plane misalignments up to 75% of sheet thickness while achieving tensile strengths close to the no-misalignment reference.
engineering_relevance: The process could improve tolerance to positioning and dimensional deviations when joining thin aluminium sheets in large structures.
method: Welded 2 mm EN AW-6082-T6 sheets using multi-pin W-FSW with continuously supplied EN AW-6082 filler wire.
Tested 1.0 and 1.5 mm misalignments with the elevated sheet on either the advancing or retreating side.
Compared joint consolidation with and without filler and evaluated tensile performance.
evidence_signal: Filler-assisted joints reached 198.8–210.0 MPa versus 208.71 MPa for the no-misalignment reference; all tensile specimens fractured outside the joining zone in the softened heat-affected zone.
watch_item: Results are limited to the investigated alloy, 2 mm sheet thickness, misalignment configurations, and tensile loading; broader production robustness remains to be established.
paper_title: Compensation of Linear Misalignments in EN AW-6082-T6 Aluminium Sheets by Multi-Pin Wire-Based Friction Stir Welding
